sanskrit: śaravegān nihatyāham astraiḥ śaravighātibhiḥ jvaladbhiḥ paramaiḥ śīghrais tān avidhyaṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: Cutting down the volleys of arrows with my blazing, supreme, swift arrow-countering weapons, I pierced them by the thousands.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ chinnāni gātrāṇi visṛjanti sma śoṇitam prāvṛṣīvātivṛṣṭāni śṛṅgāṇīva dharābhṛtām
english: Their severed limbs poured forth blood like mountain peaks drenched by torrential rain in the monsoon season.

sanskrit: indrāśanisamasparśair vegavadbhir ajihmagaiḥ madbāṇair vadhyamānās te samudvignāḥ sma dānavāḥ
english: Struck by my arrows — swift, straight-flying, and striking like Indra's thunderbolt — those dānavas were thrown into great agitation.

sanskrit: śatadhā bhinnadehāntrāḥ kṣīṇapraharaṇaujasaḥ tato nivātakavacā mām ayudhyanta māyayā
english: Their bodies and entrails shattered into hundreds of pieces, their weapon-strength exhausted, the Nivātakavacas then fought me with their powers of illusion.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca tato 'śmavarṣaṃ sumahat prādurāsīt samantataḥ nagamātrair mahāghorais tan māṃ dṛḍham apīḍayat
english: Arjuna said: Then a great shower of rocks burst forth all around — utterly terrifying boulders mountain-sized — and it pressed hard upon me.

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ vajrasaṃkāśaiḥ śarair indrāstracoditaiḥ acūrṇayaṃ vegavadbhiḥ śatadhaikaikam āhave
english: I pulverized that shower with my swift arrows charged by Indra's weapon, shattering each rock into a hundred fragments in battle.

sanskrit: cūrṇyamāne 'śmavarṣe tu pāvakaḥ samajāyata tatrāśmacūrṇam apatat pāvakaprakarā iva
english: As the rock-shower was being ground to powder, fire arose there, and the dust of those crushed stones fell like showers of sparks.

sanskrit: tato 'śmavarṣe nihate jalavarṣaṃ mahattaram dhārābhir akṣamātrābhiḥ prādurāsīn mamāntike
english: Then, when the rock-shower was destroyed, an even greater rain of water appeared near me, its streams as thick as axle-shafts.

sanskrit: nabhasaḥ pracyutā dhārās tigmavīryāḥ sahasraśaḥ āvṛṇvan sarvato vyoma diśaś copadiśas tathā
english: Streams of fierce power poured down from the sky in their thousands, covering the firmament on all sides and in every direction and quarter.

sanskrit: dhārāṇāṃ ca nipātena vāyor visphūrjitena ca garjitena ca daityānāṃ na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: From the crashing of those torrents, the howling of the wind, and the roaring of the daityas, nothing whatsoever could be discerned.

sanskrit: dhārā divi ca saṃbaddhā vasudhāyāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ vyāmohayanta māṃ tatra nipatantyo 'niśaṃ bhuvi
english: Those streams, linked between heaven and earth on every side, befuddled me there as they fell ceaselessly upon the ground.

sanskrit: tatropadiṣṭam indreṇa divyam astraṃ viśoṣaṇam dīptaṃ prāhiṇavaṃ ghoram aśuṣyat tena taj jalam
english: There, directed by Indra, I released that blazing, terrible, divine weapon of desiccation, and by it all that water was dried up.

sanskrit: hate 'śmavarṣe tu mayā jalavarṣe ca śoṣite mumucur dānavā māyām agniṃ vāyuṃ ca mānada
english: When the rock-shower was destroyed by me and the water-shower dried up, O bestower of honor, the dānavas unleashed their illusion of fire and wind.

sanskrit: tato 'ham agniṃ vyadhamaṃ salilāstreṇa sarvaśaḥ śailena ca mahāstreṇa vāyor vegam adhārayam
english: Then I extinguished the fire entirely with the water weapon, and with the great mountain-weapon I checked the force of the wind.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ pratihatāyāṃ tu dānavā yuddhadurmadāḥ prākurvan vividhā māyā yaugapadyena bhārata
english: But when that illusion was repelled, the dānavas, maddened for battle, simultaneously set loose manifold further illusions, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato varṣaṃ prādurabhūt sumahal lomaharṣaṇam astrāṇāṃ ghorarūpāṇām agner vāyos tathāśmanām
english: Then a great and hair-raising downpour of terrible weapons — of fire, of wind, and of stones — burst forth.

sanskrit: sā tu māyāmayī vṛṣṭiḥ pīḍayām āsa māṃ yudhi atha ghoraṃ tamas tīvraṃ prādurāsīt samantataḥ
english: That illusion-wrought downpour afflicted me in battle, and then a dreadful, dense darkness appeared on all sides.

sanskrit: tamasā saṃvṛte loke ghoreṇa paruṣeṇa ca turagā vimukhāś cāsan prāskhalac cāpi mātaliḥ
english: With the world enveloped in that terrible and cruel darkness, the horses turned away, and Mātali himself stumbled.

sanskrit: hastād dhiraṇmayaś cāsya pratodaḥ prāpatad bhuvi asakṛc cāha māṃ bhītaḥ kvāsīti bharatarṣabha
english: His golden goad fell from his hand to the ground, and in his fear he called to me again and again: "Where are you?" — O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: māṃ ca bhīr āviśat tīvrā tasmin vigatacetasi sa ca māṃ vigatajñānaḥ saṃtrasta idam abravīt
english: Intense fear seized me as well, and that man, his senses gone, his knowledge fled, trembling, spoke these words to me:

sanskrit: surāṇām asurāṇāṃ ca saṃgrāmaḥ sumahān abhūt amṛtārthe purā pārtha sa ca dṛṣṭo mayānagha
english: "There was once a great battle between the gods and the asuras fought for the sake of the nectar of immortality, O Pārtha, and I witnessed it, O sinless one.

sanskrit: śambarasya vadhe cāpi saṃgrāmaḥ sumahān abhūt sārathyaṃ devarājasya tatrāpi kṛtavān aham
english: At the slaying of Śambara too there was a very great battle, and there also I served as charioteer to the king of gods.

sanskrit: tathaiva vṛtrasya vadhe saṃgṛhītā hayā mayā vairocaner mayā yuddhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ cāpi sudāruṇam
english: Likewise at the slaying of Vṛtra I held the reins, and I witnessed that most terrible battle with the son of Virocana.

sanskrit: ete mayā mahāghorāḥ saṃgrāmāḥ paryupāsitāḥ na cāpi vigatajñāno bhūtapūrvo 'smi pāṇḍava
english: I have attended upon all these most dreadful battles, and never before have I lost my senses, O son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: pitāmahena saṃhāraḥ prajānāṃ vihito dhruvam na hi yuddham idaṃ yuktam anyatra jagataḥ kṣayāt
english: The destruction of all beings has surely been ordained by the Grandfather, for this battle is fit for nothing other than the annihilation of the world."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā saṃstabhyātmānam ātmanā mohayiṣyan dānavānām ahaṃ māyāmayaṃ balam
english: Hearing those words of his, I steadied myself by my own will, intending to confound the illusion-filled army of the dānavas.

sanskrit: abruvaṃ mātaliṃ bhītaṃ paśya me bhujayor balam astrāṇāṃ ca prabhāvaṃ me dhanuṣo gāṇḍivasya ca
english: I said to the frightened Mātali: "Behold the strength of my arms, the power of my weapons, and of the bow Gāṇḍīva!

sanskrit: adyāstramāyayaiteṣāṃ māyām etāṃ sudāruṇam vinihanmi tamaś cograṃ mā bhaiḥ sūta sthiro bhava
english: Today with my weapon-illusion I shall destroy this most dreadful illusion of theirs and this fierce darkness. Fear not, charioteer — be steady!"

sanskrit: evam uktvāham asṛjam astramāyāṃ narādhipa mohanīṃ sarvaśatrūṇāṃ hitāya tridivaukasām
english: Having said so, O lord of men, I released the weapon-illusion called the Bewilderer, for the benefit of all enemies and of those who dwell in the three heavens.

sanskrit: pīḍyamānāsu māyāsu tāsu tāsv asureśvarāḥ punar bahuvidhā māyāḥ prākurvann amitaujasaḥ
english: As each of their illusions was being afflicted and dispelled, the lords of the asuras, of boundless might, conjured up many further illusions in their place.

sanskrit: punaḥ prakāśam abhavat tamasā grasyate punaḥ vrajaty adarśanaṃ lokaḥ punar apsu nimajjati
english: Again there was light, then again it was swallowed by darkness; again the world went into invisibility, again it sank under water.

sanskrit: susaṃgṛhītair haribhiḥ prakāśe sati mātaliḥ vyacarat syandanāgryeṇa saṃgrāme lomaharṣaṇe
english: When there was light, Mātali, with the bay horses well in hand, drove the foremost chariot through that hair-raising battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ paryapatann ugrā nivātakavacā mayi tān ahaṃ vivaraṃ dṛṣṭvā prāhiṇvaṃ yamasādanam
english: Then the fierce Nivātakavacas fell upon me from all sides; seeing an opening, I dispatched them to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā yuddhe nivātakavacāntake nāpaśyaṃ sahasā sarvān dānavān māyayāvṛtān
english: While that battle — the destruction of the Nivātakavacas — was taking place, I suddenly could not see all those dānavas; they were shrouded in illusion.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca adṛśyamānās te daityā yodhayanti sma māyayā adṛśyān astravīryeṇa tān apy aham ayodhayam
english: Arjuna said: Though invisible, those daityas fought on by means of illusion. I too fought those invisible foes with the power of my weapons.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvamuktā viśikhāḥ samyag astrapracoditāḥ acchindann uttamāṅgāni yatra yatra sma te 'bhavan
english: Arrows released from Gāṇḍīva, properly impelled by weapon-force, severed their heads wherever those daityas happened to be.

sanskrit: tato nivātakavacā vadhyamānā mayā yudhi saṃhṛtya māyāṃ sahasā prāviśan puram ātmanaḥ
english: Then the Nivātakavacas, being slaughtered by me in battle, suddenly withdrew their illusion and retreated into their own city.

sanskrit: vyapayāteṣu daityeṣu prādurbhūte ca darśane apaśyaṃ dānavāṃs tatra hatāñ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: When the daityas had gone away and visibility had returned, I beheld dānavas lying slain there by the hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: viniṣpiṣṭāni tatraiṣāṃ śastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca kūṭaśaḥ sma pradṛśyante gātrāṇi kavacāni ca
english: Their weapons, ornaments, limbs, and armor — all shattered and crushed — lay visible there in heaps.

sanskrit: hayānāṃ nāntaraṃ hy āsīt padād vicalituṃ padam utpatya sahasā tasthur antarikṣagamās tataḥ
english: The horses had no space to move a single step; so they suddenly leaped up and stood in the sky, moving through the air.

sanskrit: tato nivātakavacā vyoma saṃchādya kevalam adṛśyā hy abhyavartanta visṛjantaḥ śiloccayān
english: Then the Nivātakavacas, completely concealing the sky, came on invisibly, hurling masses of boulders.

sanskrit: antarbhūmigatāś cānye hayānāṃ caraṇāny atha nyagṛhṇan dānavā ghorā rathacakre ca bhārata
english: Other dānavas, dreadful and underground, seized the feet of the horses and the wheels of my chariot, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vinigṛhya harīn aśvān rathaṃ ca mama yudhyataḥ sarvato mām acinvanta sarathaṃ dharaṇīdharaiḥ
english: Having seized my bay horses and my chariot as I fought, they piled upon me and my chariot from all directions with mountains.

sanskrit: parvatair upacīyadbhiḥ patamānais tathāparaiḥ sa deśo yatra vartāma guheva samapadyata
english: With mountains being heaped up and others falling, the region where we stood became like a cave.

sanskrit: parvataiś chādyamāno 'haṃ nigṛhītaiś ca vājibhiḥ agacchaṃ paramām ārtiṃ mātalis tad alakṣayat
english: Being covered by mountains and with my horses seized, I fell into the utmost distress. Mātali perceived this.

sanskrit: lakṣayitvā tu māṃ bhītam idaṃ vacanam abravīt arjunārjuna mā bhais tvaṃ vajram astram udīraya
english: Perceiving me in fear, he spoke this word: "Arjuna, Arjuna — do not be afraid! Release the vajra weapon!"

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ tasya tad vākyaṃ śrutvā vajram udīrayam devarājasya dayitaṃ vajram astraṃ narādhipa
english: Then, hearing his words, I released the vajra weapon — the beloved bolt of the king of gods — O lord of men.

sanskrit: acalaṃ sthānam āsādya gāṇḍīvam anumantrya ca amuñcaṃ vajrasaṃsparśān āyasān niśitāñ śarān
english: Taking a firm stance, I charged the Gāṇḍīva with the mantra, and released iron-sharp arrows bearing the touch of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tato māyāś ca tāḥ sarvā nivātakavacāṃś ca tān te vajracoditā bāṇā vajrabhūtāḥ samāviśan
english: Then those arrows, impelled by the vajra and having become the vajra itself, penetrated all those illusions and all those Nivātakavacas.

sanskrit: te vajravegābhihatā dānavāḥ parvatopamāḥ itaretaram āśliṣya nyapatan pṛthivītale
english: Those dānavas, mountain-like, struck by the force of the vajra, fell to the surface of the earth clinging to one another.

sanskrit: antarbhūmau tu ye 'gṛhṇan dānavā rathavājinaḥ anupraviśya tān bāṇāḥ prāhiṇvan yamasādanam
english: And those dānavas who had seized the chariot-horses underground — the arrows followed them in and sent them to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: hatair nivātakavacair nirastaiḥ parvatopamaiḥ samācchādyata deśaḥ sa vikīrṇair iva parvataiḥ
english: With the Nivātakavacas slain and their mountain-like bodies strewn about, that region was covered as if with scattered mountains.

sanskrit: na hayānāṃ kṣatiḥ kā cin na rathasya na mātaleḥ mama cādṛśyata tadā tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: No harm whatsoever was seen to have befallen the horses, nor the chariot, nor Mātali, nor myself — and that seemed like a wonder.

sanskrit: tato māṃ prahasan rājan mātaliḥ pratyabhāṣata naitad arjuna deveṣu tvayi vīryaṃ yadīkṣyate
english: Then Mātali, smiling, addressed me, O king: "This prowess that is seen in you, Arjuna, is not seen even among the gods."

sanskrit: hateṣv asurasaṃgheṣu dārās teṣāṃ tu sarvaśaḥ prākrośan nagare tasmin yathā śaradi lakṣmaṇāḥ
english: When the hosts of asuras were slain, their wives wailed throughout that city, like female deer in the autumn season.

sanskrit: tato mātalinā sārdham ahaṃ tat puram abhyayām trāsayan rathaghoṣeṇa nivātakavacastriyaḥ
english: Then, together with Mātali, I drove toward that city, terrifying the women of the Nivātakavacas with the thunder of my chariot.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā daśasāhasrān mayūrasadṛśān hayān rathaṃ ca ravisaṃkāśaṃ prādravan gaṇaśaḥ striyaḥ
english: Seeing those ten-thousand horses resembling peacocks and the chariot blazing like the sun, the women fled in groups.

sanskrit: tābhir ābharaṇaiḥ śabdas trāsitābhiḥ samīritaḥ śilānām iva śaileṣu patantīnām abhūt tadā
english: The sound made by their ornaments as they fled in terror was like that of rocks falling upon rocky mountains.

sanskrit: vitrastā daityanāryas tāḥ svāni veśmāny athāviśan bahuratnavicitrāni śātakumbhamayāni ca
english: Those terrified women of the daityas then retreated into their own dwellings — richly adorned with many jewels and fashioned of gold.

sanskrit: tad adbhutākāram ahaṃ dṛṣṭvā nagaram uttamam viśiṣṭaṃ devanagarād apṛcchaṃ mātaliṃ tataḥ
english: Seeing that most excellent city of wondrous appearance, superior to the city of the gods, I then questioned Mātali about it.

sanskrit: idam evaṃvidhaṃ kasmād devatā nāviśanty uta puraṃdarapurād dhīdaṃ viśiṣṭam iti lakṣaye
english: "Why do the gods not inhabit such a place as this? I perceive that this city surpasses even the city of Purandara."

sanskrit: mātalir uvāca āsīd idaṃ purā pārtha devarājasya naḥ puram tato nivātakavacair itaḥ pracyāvitāḥ surāḥ
english: Mātali said: This city was formerly ours, O Pārtha — it belonged to the king of gods. Then the gods were driven away from here by the Nivātakavacas.

sanskrit: tapas taptvā mahat tīvraṃ prasādya ca pitāmaham idaṃ vṛtaṃ nivāsāya devebhyaś cābhayaṃ yudhi
english: Having performed great and severe austerities and having propitiated the Grandfather, they requested this as their dwelling and immunity from the gods in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakreṇa bhagavān svayambhūr abhicoditaḥ vidhattāṃ bhagavān atrety ātmano hitakāmyayā
english: Then the blessed Indra, for his own welfare's sake, urged the blessed Self-born One: "Let the Lord ordain here" — meaning their end.

sanskrit: tata ukto bhagavatā diṣṭam atreti vāsavaḥ bhavitāntas tvam evaiṣāṃ dehenānyena vṛtrahan
english: Then Vāsava was told by the blessed one: "It is ordained here — you yourself, O Vṛtrahan, in another body, shall be their end."

sanskrit: tata eṣāṃ vadhārthāya śakro 'strāṇi dadau tava na hi śakyāḥ surair hantuṃ ya ete nihatās tvayā
english: Then, for the purpose of their destruction, Śakra gave you those weapons — for those whom you have slain could not be slain by the gods.

sanskrit: kālasya pariṇāmena tatas tvam iha bhārata eṣām antakaraḥ prāptas tat tvayā ca kṛtaṃ tathā
english: By the ripening of time, O Bhārata, you have arrived here as the one who brings their end, and you have done precisely that.

sanskrit: dānavānāṃ vināśārthaṃ mahāstrāṇāṃ mahad balam grāhitas tvaṃ mahendreṇa puruṣendra tad uttamam
english: For the destruction of the dānavas, the great Indra caused you, O lord among men, to receive the great power of the great weapons — that supreme gift.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca tataḥ praviśya nagaraṃ dānavāṃś ca nihatya tān punar mātalinā sārdham agacchaṃ devasadma tat
english: Arjuna said: Then, having entered the city and slain those dānavas, I again departed for the divine abode, together with Mātali.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca nivartamānena mayā mahad dṛṣṭaṃ tato 'param puraṃ kāmacaraṃ divyaṃ pāvakārkasamaprabham
english: Arjuna said: As I was returning, I then saw another great city — divine, moving at will, blazing like fire and sun together.

sanskrit: drumai ratnamayaiś caitrair bhāsvaraiś ca patatribhiḥ paulomaiḥ kālakeyaiś ca nityahṛṣṭair adhiṣṭhitam
english: It was inhabited by jeweled, variegated trees with radiant birds, and by the Paulomas and Kālakeys, ever joyful.

sanskrit: gopurāṭṭālakopetaṃ caturdvāraṃ durāsadam sarvaratnamayaṃ divyam adbhutopamadarśanam drumaiḥ puṣpaphalopetair divyaratnamayair vṛtam
english: Adorned with gateways and towers, with four gates, impregnable, made entirely of precious gems, divine, wondrous to behold, encircled by trees bearing flowers and fruits fashioned of divine jewels.

sanskrit: tathā patatribhir divyais upetaṃ sumanoharaiḥ asurair nityamuditaiḥ śūlarṣṭimusalāyudhaiḥ cāpamudgarahastaiś ca sragvibhiḥ sarvato vṛtam
english: Filled likewise with divine birds of exquisite beauty, and surrounded on all sides by asuras forever rejoicing, bearing tridents, pikes, pestles, bows, and clubs in their hands, and wearing garlands.

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ prekṣya daityānāṃ puram adbhutadarśanam apṛcchaṃ mātaliṃ rājan kim idaṃ dṛśyateti vai
english: Beholding that city of the daityas, wondrous in appearance, I asked Mātali, O king: "What is this that is seen here?"

sanskrit: mātalir uvāca pulomā nāma daiteyī kālakā ca mahāsurī divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ te ceratuḥ paramaṃ tapaḥ tapaso 'nte tatas tābhyāṃ svayambhūr adadād varam
english: Mātali said: A daitya woman named Pulomā and the great asura woman Kālakā practiced supreme austerities for a divine thousand years; at the end of their austerities the Self-born One granted them a boon.

sanskrit: agṛhṇītāṃ varaṃ te tu sutānām alpaduḥkhatām avadhyatāṃ ca rājendra surarākṣasapannagaiḥ
english: Those two chose as their boon the freedom of their sons from great suffering, and their invulnerability to gods, rākṣasas, and serpents, O king of kings.

sanskrit: ramaṇīyaṃ puraṃ cedaṃ khacaraṃ sukṛtaprabham sarvaratnaiḥ samuditaṃ durdharṣam amarair api sayakṣagandharvagaṇaiḥ pannagāsurarākṣasaiḥ
english: This beautiful city, sky-moving, radiant with accumulated merit, replete with all manner of gems, impregnable even by the immortals together with yakshas, gandharvas, serpents, asuras, and rākṣasas —

sanskrit: sarvakāmaguṇopetaṃ vītaśokam anāmayam brahmaṇā bharataśreṣṭha kālakeyakṛte kṛtam
english: — furnished with every desired quality, free from sorrow and disease, was made by Brahmā, O best of Bhāratas, for the sake of the Kālakeys.

sanskrit: tad etat khacaraṃ divyaṃ caraty amaravarjitam paulomādhyuṣitaṃ vīra kālakeyaiś ca dānavaiḥ
english: This divine sky-roaming city, from which the immortals are excluded, is inhabited, O hero, by the Paulomas and the Kālakey dānavas.

sanskrit: hiraṇyapuram ity etat khyāyate nagaraṃ mahat rakṣitaṃ kālakeyaiś ca paulomaiś ca mahāsuraiḥ
english: This great city is known as Hiraṇyapura — the Golden City — and it is guarded by the Kālakeys and the Paulomas, those mighty asuras.
